note: Draft data for the ten cards that act on Places. No pictures. 'cost' is the cost the test games support (results.txt); 'costTested' is the cost the card has in cards-places.js, where the games started from, when the two differ. 'does' is the kind of thing the card does, in the owner's words. 'sure': 3 well attested, 2 the usual account, 1 a story told about the person, and the sentence says so.

cards.does: look at the top of your stack for a Place for your Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: When Pachacuti arrives, look at the top three Places of your stack. You may lay one of them at your Gate or your Outpost in place of the Place that is there. Put the others under your stack.
cards.fact: He turned the small kingdom of Cusco into the Inca empire and rebuilt its capital in stone, and Machu Picchu was most likely built as his estate.
cards.domain: Land: a ruler who chooses where his people build.
cards.line: Legacy Line from Machu Picchu and from Qhapaq Ñan

cards.does: look through your whole stack for a Place for your Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: When Al-Idrisi arrives, you may look through your whole Place stack, choose one Place and lay it at your Gate or your Outpost in place of the Place that is there. Then shuffle your stack.
cards.fact: At the court of Roger II in Palermo he spent some fifteen years questioning travellers, and in 1154 he finished a map of the known world with a book describing every part of it.
cards.domain: Routes: knowing the land, the map that shows every Place there is.

cards.tx: When Constantine arrives, you may turn up the top Place of your stack and lay it at the Crossroads in place of the Place that is there.
cards.fact: In 330 he made the old Greek town of Byzantium, where Europe meets Asia, his new capital, and it was called Constantinople after him.
cards.domain: Law: a new capital moves the seat of government.

cards.does: force the other player to replace their Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: When William arrives at the other player's Gate or Outpost, you may make them replace that Place with the top Place of their stack.
cards.fact: After he won at Hastings in 1066 he gave the land of England to his own followers, and his great survey of 1086, the Domesday Book, shows almost none of it still in English hands.

cards.does: bring back a Place that was replaced
cards.tx: When Christopher Wren arrives, you may take a Place from your Place discard pile and lay it at your Gate or your Outpost in place of the Place that is there.
cards.fact: After the Great Fire of London in 1666 he rebuilt St Paul's Cathedral and more than fifty of the city's churches.
cards.domain: Culture: what was lost is built again.

cards.cap: Sinope and Corinth, c. 404 to 323 BC
cards.tx: The Place where Diogenes stands has no rule.
cards.fact: He lived in Athens and Corinth with next to nothing and mocked wealth, rank and custom. The story goes that when Alexander offered him any favour, he asked the king to stand out of his sunlight.
cards.domain: Ideas: a man no wonder could impress.
cards.line: Legacy of Socrates would stretch the record (he studied under Antisthenes, a follower of Socrates): left off.

cards.does: force a player to replace their Gate or Outpost
cards.tx: Choose a Gate or an Outpost, yours or the other player's. Its owner replaces that Place with the top Place of their stack.
cards.fact: An earthquake in 226 BC threw down the Colossus of Rhodes, which had stood for little more than fifty years.

cards.tx: Lay Vesuvius on a Place. That Place has no rule for as long as Vesuvius lies on it. Vesuvius is discarded when the Place is replaced.
cards.fact: In AD 79 it buried the trading town of Pompeii in a day, and the town lay under the ash for nearly seventeen hundred years.
cards.domain: Commerce silenced: a busy town buried.

cards.tx: Turn up the top Place of your stack and lay it at the Crossroads in place of the Place that is there.
cards.fact: Vasco da Gama reached India by sea around Africa in 1498, and within a few years a large share of the spice trade that had made Venice and Cairo rich went by the new route.
cards.domain: Commerce: a new route moves the trade.
cards.line: Legacy Line from the Cape of Good Hope

cards.tx: The other player's cards cannot replace your Gate or your Outpost, and cannot take away their rules.
cards.fact: In Babylonia a grant of land was carved on a stone, with curses on anyone who moved the boundary or took the land.
cards.domain: Law: the land is yours because it is written.
